channel.title: Essays — Vadim Vladymtsev
channel.description: Original essays by Vadim Vladymtsev on software architecture, AI at work, shared understanding, project communities and authorship.

item.title: Revising an Architecture I Designed
item.description: What rebuilding part of my own microservices application taught me about engineering responsibility, migration costs, and professional trust.

item.title: Who Gets the Time AI Saves?
item.description: AI can make a task faster. The value depends on who receives the time saved and what the company enables them to do with it.

item.title: Shared Understanding Takes Work
item.description: What coaching a competitive programming team taught me about explaining ideas, sharing context, and helping strong people work independently.

item.title: What Happens After the Applause
item.description: A startup competition creates opportunities. Teams still need a way to use them. My view of support after the final, informed by StartLab.

item.title: Recognizing Myself in My Work
item.description: Personal taste, thoughtful details, and shared credit: why I want to understand my own choices and return to the things I have made.
